resources.string: This removes hermes\\' bundled desktop-automation tool (cua-driver). It is only used in that kind of session, and it won\\'t come back on its own — run hermes pm install once in the terminal to get it back (needs network, takes a while).
Browser tools (agent-browser / chromium) are not removed — hermes needs them to open web pages, so they stay.

ffmpeg isn\\'t included either: it\\'s a required package for hermes, and removing it makes hermes report \"install out of sync\" on every start (it doesn\\'t accept the copy bundled with the system layer).
Not removed: python / node / uv / npm / ripgrep runtimes, the dependency environment, memory, the hermes installation itself, system files, or any of your data.
Clean installer script cache (re-downloads next install)
This deletes the cached installer scripts in the shared agents/scripts folder, the checksums the app keeps, and the copy in the terminal.
The scripts are only tens of KB — this isn\\'t about freeing space, it\\'s about making the next install download a clean copy (if a reinstall keeps hitting the same failure, start here).
Not removed: the agent ledger installed.json, installed agents and toolchains, logs, or the knowledge base.
Cleared %1$d cached script files (freed %2$d MB); the next install will re-download them
Location: %1$s (cache = package cache, logs = logs, agents = scripts & ledger; rootfs and opencode are installers)

Package cache (very low risk): downloads from npm / uv / apt, cleaned in the terminal so you can watch it. Temp files (low risk): leftovers in the temp folder untouched for over a day; no terminal needed, and the app also clears automatically when it exceeds 500 MB at startup. Toolchains, system files and your data are never touched.
The environment isn\\'t installed yet, so there\\'s nothing to clean in the terminal
Deletes about %1$d MB of leftovers in the temp folder (untouched for over a day).\n\nTerminal sessions, build caches and lock files are not deleted, and your data is untouched.
These caches will be deleted (they can be re-downloaded or regenerated):
⚠️ A terminal session is running: if it is installing dependencies right now, cleaning may interrupt that install (anything already installed is unaffected).
Not removed: installed agents and toolchains (hermes/tools, Python/Node), the dependency environment and memory, config files, system files, or your own files. These caches re-download when needed.

Every reinstall of the dependency environment leaves an old copy (hundreds of MB), and the record only points at the newest one — this deletes the ones nothing refers to. The one in use and the newest one are kept.
Not removed: the dependency environment in use, memory, installed toolchains, system files. hermes reinstalls when you need to go back (requires network).
No old dependency files to clean
Clean old version cache (keeps the current version)
Old versions you can go back to (only the latest 2 installers are kept)
Will reinstall system files from %1$s (a few minutes). Logins and your workspace are kept.
Roll back: reinstall from local installer %1$s (no download)
Unpacking (no detailed progress — stay on this page or watch the notification)…
Rollback done: switched back to %1$s, takes effect after reopening the terminal (no download)
Tap \"Install environment\" on the home screen to set up Debian; then tap \"Install\" on any agent you want.
Sign in inside each agent (it keeps its own credentials), and it is ready to use.

Open the \"Terminal\" tab and type an agent command (claude / hermes / agy). OpenCode is built into \"Taiji\" and works out of the box. A separate opencode you install in the terminal is a different copy — the two do not interfere.
Use \"Repair environment\" above to unpack it again — your logins are kept.
How do I update an agent?
Re-run the install command in the terminal. To update the system, use \"Check for updates\".
Output goes into the workspace folder (by default Download/证道 on your phone).

zhengdao-log.txt is this run; timestamped archives keep at most 20 files / 20 MB, oldest deleted first (a clean run is never deleted); errors.log records error lines only. Open them with a file manager, or send them to us to look into a problem.
The last run hit an error; the log was kept (copy it and send it to us).
Deleted %1$d old logs, kept the latest 3
This run hasn\'t written a log yet. Log folder: %1$s (open it with a file manager)
Agent output goes into this folder (visible in your file manager)
The readme hasn\'t been generated yet — open the terminal once and it will appear in the knowledge base folder.\n\nLocation: %1$s
Couldn\'t read it — open the readme (说明.md) directly in the knowledge base folder.

① App launch: Settings → Apps → App launch → Zhengdao → turn off "Auto-manage", then allow auto-start / linked start / background activity
② Battery: Settings → Battery → More battery settings → Zhengdao → set to "Don't optimize"
③ Task lock: in Recents find the Zhengdao card, swipe down for the lock icon and tap it
④ If it exits on its own: Developer options → make sure "Don't keep activities" is off

Honor is fairly lenient with background services: keep the \"Session running\" notification visible and lock the task, and it will stay alive in the background. If the system does kill it, reopening the terminal takes you back to where you left off.
One tap: set Zhengdao to \"Don\'t optimize\"
Set it manually in Settings → Battery optimization
Not implemented yet — Zhengdao runs Debian without root
